question: A 25-year-old man with known squamosal CSOM develops sudden onset facial nerve palsy (LMN type) with no other symptoms. What is the most likely mechanism?

answers.text: Haematogenous spread of infection to the facial nerve

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Haematogenous spread is not the primary mechanism in CSOM-related facial palsy. The facial nerve in the temporal bone runs through the facial nerve canal adjacent to the middle ear; cholesteatoma erodes directly into this bony canal by enzymatic bone resorption.

answers.text: Direct bone erosion by cholesteatoma into the bony facial nerve canal

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Cholesteatoma erodes bone by enzymatic action (collagenases, osteoclast activation). The facial nerve canal — particularly at the second genu where it runs lateral to the posterior semicircular canal — is a common site of erosion. Direct pressure and infection produce LMN facial palsy. This is an indication for urgent surgical exploration.

Incorrect. Lateral (sigmoid) sinus thrombosis causes systemic sepsis, spiking fever, and headache. While sinus thrombosis can occasionally extend and affect adjacent structures, direct bone erosion of the facial nerve canal is the far more common mechanism for facial palsy in cholesteatoma.

answers.text: Inflammatory oedema from a Bezold abscess compressing the facial nerve

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A Bezold abscess is an extracranial complication where infection perforates the mastoid tip and tracks into the neck along the sternocleidomastoid muscle. It does not directly cause facial nerve palsy. The facial nerve is at risk from intratemporal erosion, not cervical abscess compression.

overallFeedback.feedback: In CSOM, facial nerve palsy is caused by direct enzymatic bone erosion of the facial nerve canal by cholesteatoma. This is an intratemporal complication requiring urgent surgical decompression.
Correct. Cholesteatoma causes facial palsy by direct bone erosion into the facial nerve canal. This is a surgical emergency — decompression is required.
